description: Named Aero Hand poses on voice: 'Jarvis peace' / 'peace sign', 'flip me off', 'rock on', 'surf's up' (shaka), and 'lululil' (unclear transcription — maybe 'I love you' ASL; confirm with Jake). The voice session runs one deterministic command that moves the hand to the pose quickly. Build on third_party/aero_hand/scripts/performance.py (SDK set_joint_positions, 7 joints, port auto-detected; LEFT hand). Make it easy to add poses.

results.identified_issue: Number poses are hand-authored joint vectors, not tuned on camera. 3 uses the mainland OK-style form with performance.py's thumb-to-index PINCHES[0] values; 7 averages PINCHES[0] and [1] with index/middle at 50; 9 is index at 50 (the single index tendon can't make a true hook); 10 is a fist because crossed index fingers needs two hands. 666 and six share shaka's joints. norm() now keeps digits so '7' and '10' match. Count aliases: 'count to ten', 'count to 10', 'count', 'count in chinese'. Each number glides at MOVE_S 0.7 s, then holds HOLD_S 1.0 s, so the whole count takes about 18.5 s. hand_speed.limit() still runs on connect. The voice routing lives in the ~/.claude/projects/-Users-jakeschantz memory hand-named-poses.md, which I updated.
results.summary: Added the 666 sign, Chinese hand numbers one to ten, and 'count to ten' (about a second on each number) to pose.sh
results.detailed_description: pose.sh now has the 666 sign (thumb and pinky up; 'lululil', 'liu liu liu' and 'six six six' all map to it) and the Chinese one-hand numbers: 'pose.sh seven' (or 7, or qi) shows one number, and 'pose.sh count to ten' runs 1 to 10. Each number glides in (0.7 s) and then holds for 1 s. The 50% hand_speed.limit() cap is unchanged. Shapes: 1 index; 2 index and middle; 3 is the OK style, with the thumb on the index tip and the other three up (the thumb values are copied from the pinch in performance.py); 4 is four fingers with the thumb tucked; 5 open; 6 thumb and pinky; 7 is the thumb, index and middle pinched with the ring and pinky curled; 8 is thumb and index (the L); 9 is the index half-bent (the single index tendon can't do a real hook); 10 is a fist. I ran 'count to ten', then 666, then open on your hand. All of them went through in about 18.5 s and it's open now, but I didn't watch it, so 3, 7 and 9 are the ones most likely to need tuning. I also updated the voice-session memory so 'Jarvis seven' and 'Jarvis count to ten' run pose.sh, and the README.

results.summary: Added pose.sh: one command moves the hand straight to peace, flip off, rock on, shaka, I love you, fist or open
results.detailed_description: New third_party/aero_hand/scripts/pose.sh <name> (wrapper for pose.py). It finds the port itself, sends the pose once with set_joint_positions (3 times, 20 ms apart, so a stalled USB frame can't leave it unmoved), and exits, so the hand jumps there as fast as the servos go, with no song and no interpolation. Names match loosely: 'Surf's up!', 'surfs up', 'hang loose' and 'shaka' all work, as do 'peace sign', 'flip me off', 'middle finger', 'rock on', 'horns'. I guessed 'lululil' means the ASL 'I love you' (thumb, index and pinky out), so that's 'i love you' / 'ily' / 'love you'. Tell me if you meant something else. Rock on is the horns with the thumb tucked over the curled middle and ring fingers. Note that performance.py's 'rock on' leaves the thumb out, so it's really the I-love-you sign. The thumb positions are hardcoded: tucked = [90, 45, 60], copied from the routine's peace sign; out = all zeros. Adding a pose is one line in POSES. I also added a memory note for the voice session ('Jarvis <pose>' → pose.sh) and a README line. Your hand was plugged in: my test of "Surf's up!" really moved it, so it's sitting in shaka right now. I haven't seen the other poses on the hand. Try: pose.sh peace, pose.sh flip me off, pose.sh rock on, pose.sh i love you, pose.sh open.

results.notes: Jake: 'lululil' is the Chinese 666 sign (liù liù liù, 'that's cool'): thumb and pinky up, other fingers down (same shape as the 6 sign / shaka). Also add Chinese one-hand counting 1 to 10 as poses, so 'Jarvis count to ten' runs 1..10 and 'Jarvis seven' shows one number: 1 index; 2 index+middle; 3 middle+ring+pinky (OK-style, thumb touching index) or the index+middle+ring form; 4 four fingers, thumb folded; 5 open hand; 6 thumb+pinky; 7 fingertips pinched together; 8 thumb+index (L / pistol); 9 index hooked; 10 fist (or crossed index fingers, which one hand can't do, so use a fist). Check each against a reference for the common mainland forms.
